target_customer: Owners of used construction machines (contractors and small construction companies) who want to resell them, and international used equipment dealers who bid on them
problem: Selling a used construction machine is slow and opaque for owners, who lack access to an international dealer network and a standard way to document machine condition.
business_model: Marketplace and remarketing service for used construction machines (inspection app plus dealer bidding; fee structure not stated in sources)
product_category: Used construction equipment marketplace and inspection software

founders.name: Steffen Schweiger
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists Steffen and Christian Schweiger. A press profile surfaced in search says Steffen and Niklas met at the construction OEM PERI where they led equipment sales projects; education was not found.

founders.name: Christian Schweiger
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. No background found.

founders.name: Niklas Fritz
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in press material surfaced by search (lectura.press); not on the YC page.

competitors.name: IronPlanet allEquip (Ritchie Bros)
competitors.what: Online marketplace for used construction equipment with buy now prices

competitors.name: Equipment Experts
competitors.what: Pay for performance online marketplace for used trucking, construction and agriculture equipment from Randall-Reilly

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace plus a mobile inspection app that collects machine condition data is standard engineering; the hard part is the dealer network and trust, not the technology.

defensibility.rationale: A verified international dealer buyer network and inspection data can build liquidity, but incumbent auction houses and OEM platforms offer similar listings.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent auction houses already ran online used equipment marketplaces and Liebherr later launched its own used equipment marketplace (date not confirmed). No acquisition of Machine26 was found.

market_need_then: Used construction machines are traded through local dealers and auctions; the company's pitch is that small owners cannot reach international buyers easily. No dated demand statistics were found.

branding.name_origin: The company site says the 26 refers to iron's position in the periodic table, iron being the main component of construction machines.
branding.domain_note: Uses machine26.com; no acquisition story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: plain and practical: simple, efficient, secure

branding.brand_signature: The periodic table number 26 for iron

brand_strength.rationale: Only a few trade press mentions were found and no community or merch; the name has a clear story but is a niche B2B brand.

outcome_analysis: Machine26 remains active as a small Berlin team of about 12 per YC. No outcome event such as an acquisition or shutdown was found in a dedicated search. Public funding information is limited to database entries of roughly 125 thousand to 190 thousand dollars, so the company appears capital light, but this cannot be confirmed. It announced a partnership with Cemex Germany in 2023 according to search results, which suggests some commercial traction.
notes: Funding unverified: Seedtable lists a pre-seed of about 125 to 130 thousand dollars (Jan 2021, YC) and Caplight lists about 189 thousand dollars total with a June 2022 accelerator entry; both are aggregators, so no round is recorded. The site lists YC, IBB, EU ESF and BER as supporters without stating their nature. The Klarx funding news in search results concerns a different company. Competitor traction and funding not stated in the sources.
